routes.dispositionReason: ADM-033 compatibility alias. The customer roster moved to /v1/admin/customers because the population is Organization.kind = 'CUSTOMER', which EXCLUDES the internal 1:1 bootstrap container every workspace owns — and calling the surface 'organizations' is what made counting those containers look reasonable for as long as it did. This path is registered with the SAME requirePlatformAdmin gate and the SAME handler so no existing consumer breaks mid-flight; the web console calls the canonical path and next.config.js permanently redirects the page route. Zero product consumers is therefore the CORRECT state for it.

routes.dispositionEvidence: BILLING PERSONAL/ORGANIZATION MODEL (2026-08-28). reg services/api/src/routes/teams.routes.ts app.post("/v1/teams", { preHandler: requireAuthAndLegal }) — the handler's first statement is `await assertUserCanCreateAnotherOwnedWorkspace(ownerUserId)`, which ALWAYS throws 409 WORKSPACE_CREATION_NOT_SELF_SERVICE. The creation body it guarded (organization.create + grantOrganizationMembership + team.create in one transaction under an advisory lock) was DELETED rather than left unreachable, which is why services/api/test/p1-workspace-kind.test.ts and services/api/test/phase-2-domain-classification.test.ts now assert the ABSENCE of any team.create in this file, and services/api/test/phase-12-arch-002-workspace-kind-authority.test.ts no longer lists it as a workspace writer. WHY IT REFUSES: checkout has ONE subject and it is the person (assertCheckoutTarget refuses any teamId with CHECKOUT_TARGET_NOT_SUPPORTED), so a workspace created here could never be paid for — it would resolve FREE permanently and the shared-workspace admission rule in billing-enforcement.service.ts would refuse every piece of evidence recorded in it; returning 201 for something permanently unusable is worse than refusing. ZERO PRODUCT CONSUMERS, deliberately: apps/web/components/workspace-admin/CreateWorkspaceCard.tsx was its only caller and was DELETED in the same change, because a control for a capability the server refuses is a button that always fails. EXISTING Owned Workspaces are untouched — not archived, not downgraded, not hidden — and multi-workspace tenancy remains real, created by Enterprise provisioning against a contract on a path that never used this route.
routes.dispositionReason: Self-service workspace creation was removed with the commercial allowance that permitted it; every path through the route now refuses, and it is retained so a stale client gets a code-bearing explanation instead of a 404.
